title: Eighty minutes of Paris — the things he asked for
subtopic: 4 — Paris: what he did not see
learning_goal: Know the two places Passepartout names and the one Verne does not; feel that the traveller is the one who gets to stop.

narration.script:
Here is the card. A clock, and eighty minutes. Twenty past seven at the Gare du Nord, twenty to nine at the Gare de Lyon, four kilometres of Paris in between, in the rain.

In the novel, Passepartout names two things he wishes he could see. Neither is on the road between the stations. Both are on the card, in grey — with a third that is ours. Tap any of them.
narration.after_script: He asked for a cemetery and a circus. We can go to one of them.

media.note: SPEC (G-205). Card title 'Eighty minutes of Paris'. A clock face with two hands set at 7:20 and 8:40. Under it, three lines in the Day-1 card style: '7:20 am — Gare du Nord' / '≈ 4 km across the city, by cab, in driving rain' / '8:40 am — Gare de Lyon'. Then THREE NAMES IN GHOSTED TYPE, tappable, in any order: 'Père-Lachaise' with Verne's line beneath it — "How I regret not having seen once more Père la Chaise…" (Towle's spelling INSIDE the quotation only; house spelling Père-Lachaise everywhere else); 'the circus in the Champs-Élysées' with "…and the circus in the Champs Elysées!"; and third, unlabelled until tapped, 'the Tuileries', with the caption 'he does not mention this one'. Footer line: 'Neither of the two he named is on the road between the stations.' THE CARD MUST BE FULLY LEGIBLE WITH NO PHOTOGRAPHS AT ALL — the four reveal plates (M-256 Tuileries in ruins, M-257 Père-Lachaise / Mur des Fédérés, M-258 Cirque des Champs-Élysées engraving, M-259 rue du Cirque today) are REQUESTED, not landed, and have no refs in the manifest, so they are deliberately NOT media entries here. When the Content Preparer lands them, add each as an image with start_s at its tap and a note, and the card loses nothing if they never arrive. Facts: F-53, F-55, F-83, F-84, F-85.

interaction.prompt: Tap a name. Any order — there is no right answer here.

options.feedback: The cemetery. He wants to see it once more — he is a Parisian. Seventeen months before this morning, against its south-east wall, about a hundred and forty-seven Communards were shot and buried in a common grave.
A real building on the Champs-Élysées, from 1841. The Empress's circus until the Empire fell in 1870; gone by 1900. All that is left is the street name — and he was a circus rider himself.

The one he does not name. The palace in the middle of Paris burned in May 1871 and stood as an empty shell behind a fence for eleven years. A Frenchman wrote this book that year. He does not mention it.
